title: Microsoft Entra users and groups: creation, properties and dynamic membership
learningObjective: Create users and groups, one at a time or in bulk. Pick the right group type and membership type. Write dynamic membership rules. Manage user and group properties.
foundation: Microsoft Entra ID is the directory that stores your organisation's users and groups and signs them in to Azure, Microsoft 365 and other apps.
A user account has a sign-in name (the user principal name, such as ana@contoso.com) and properties such as department, job title and usage location.
Groups collect users so you can grant access or licences once instead of per person. Security groups are for access; Microsoft 365 groups add a shared mailbox, calendar and files.
Membership can be Assigned (you add people) or Dynamic (a rule such as 'department equals Sales' decides automatically).
engineer: Where users come from: cloud-only users are created directly in Entra ID; synced users come from your on-premises Active Directory through Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, so you change their details on-premises, not in the portal; guests are people from other organisations (userType is Guest).
Ways to create users: the portal (New user > Create new user); bulk create, by uploading the portal's CSV template; Microsoft Graph PowerShell (New-MgUser); Azure CLI (az ad user create).
Deleting users: a deleted user goes to the recycle bin (soft delete). You can restore them for 30 days.
Group types: Security groups give access (Azure roles, licences, Conditional Access, apps); Microsoft 365 groups are for teamwork (shared mailbox, calendar, files) but can also give access.

Membership types: Assigned, where you add people by hand; Dynamic user, where a rule picks the users; Dynamic device, where a rule picks devices (security groups only). You can change the membership type later.

Groups that hold admin roles: to give a group a Microsoft Entra role, create it with 'Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group' set to Yes (isAssignableToRole). You can't switch this on later. These groups use Assigned membership only.

Dynamic rules: a rule reads a user property and compares it, for example user.department -eq "Sales". Compare with -eq, -ne, -startsWith, -contains or -match. Join rules with -and, -or, -not. You can't add members by hand to a dynamic group. Updates are not instant; in big tenants they can take a while.
Licence for dynamic groups: every user who is in a dynamic group needs Microsoft Entra ID P1.

Who can do what: User Administrator manages users and groups; Groups Administrator manages groups only; a group owner can change members of an Assigned group; Azure RBAC roles such as Owner or Contributor give no rights in the directory.

Properties to remember: usageLocation, which must be set before you give a licence directly; accountEnabled, set it to No to block sign-in; department, jobTitle and companyName, which dynamic rules often use; manager.
PowerShell: the old AzureAD and MSOnline modules are retired. Use Microsoft Graph PowerShell.

animation.caption: Edit a dynamic rule or a user's department and watch membership flows update.

example.title: New starters and team moves, handled by a rule
body: HR sets each person's department when they join or move. A dynamic security group called Sales has the rule user.department -eq "Sales". That group gets access to the CRM resource group and the Sales licences.

Chen moves from Sales to Engineering. HR changes Chen's department. The rule removes Chen from Sales, and Chen's Sales access and licences go with it. No admin touches the group. Chen is a synced user, so the department is changed in on-premises AD and then syncs to the cloud.

prerequisites: Microsoft Entra ID P1 for dynamic groups
limits: Deleted users can be restored for 30 days
No manual members in dynamic groups
Role-assignable setting must be chosen at group creation
portal: Microsoft Entra admin center > Users > New user > Create new user: UPN, display name, password, then Properties (department, usage location) and Assignments (groups, roles).
Users > Bulk operations > Bulk create: download the CSV template, fill it in, upload, and monitor the result in Bulk operation results.
Groups > New group: Group type, name, Membership type (Assigned / Dynamic user / Dynamic device). For dynamic, select 'Add dynamic query' and validate the rule against sample users.
Users > Deleted users: restore within 30 days.
configuration.cli:
az ad user create --display-name "Ana Silva" --user-principal-name ana@contoso.com \
  --password '<initial-password>' --force-change-password-next-sign-in true
az ad group create --display-name "Ops team" --mail-nickname opsteam
az ad group member add --group "Ops team" --member-id $(az ad user show --id ana@contoso.com --query id -o tsv)
az ad group member list --group "Ops team" --query "[].userPrincipalName" -o tsv
configuration.powershell:
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All','Group.ReadWrite.All'
New-MgUser -DisplayName 'Ana Silva' -UserPrincipalName 'ana@contoso.com' -MailNickname 'ana' -AccountEnabled `
  -PasswordProfile @{ Password = '<initial-password>'; ForceChangePasswordNextSignIn = $true } -Department 'Sales' -UsageLocation 'PT'
Update-MgUser -UserId 'ana@contoso.com' -JobTitle 'Account Manager'
New-MgGroup -DisplayName 'Sales' -MailEnabled:$false -MailNickname 'sales' -SecurityEnabled `
  -GroupTypes 'DynamicMembership' -MembershipRule '(user.department -eq "Sales")' -MembershipRuleProcessingState 'On'

lab.objective: Use properties and dynamic rules to automate group membership, and see the limits of dynamic groups.
steps: On Users & groups, change Ben's department to Sales and watch him join the dynamic group.
Change the rule to include guests (-or user.userType -eq "Guest") and save it.
Try to add Ben manually to the dynamic group, then add him to the assigned SSPR pilot group.

lab.cost: None. In a real tenant, dynamic groups need Entra ID P1 licences.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't edit a user's department in the portal.
troubleshooting.cause: The user is synced from on-premises AD, so AD is the source of their details.
troubleshooting.fix: Change it in AD. It reaches the cloud at the next sync.

troubleshooting.symptom: A user isn't in the dynamic group their department should match.
troubleshooting.cause: The rule has a typo or a spacing or case difference, or the update hasn't finished yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Use 'Validate rules' on the group to test that user, and check the group's processing status.
Change the rule or the user's details, or change the group to Assigned.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't give an Entra role to a group.
troubleshooting.cause: The group wasn't created as role-assignable, and that can't be changed later.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a new group with 'Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group' set to Yes.

comparisons.difference: In AD, a group inside a group passes on access. In Entra ID, group-based licensing and some other features ignore groups inside groups, and only direct members count.
AWS IAM groups can't contain other groups and have no dynamic rules. Company staff usually sign in through IAM Identity Center instead.

misconceptions.myth: A subscription Owner can create Entra users.
misconceptions.reality: No. Azure roles only cover Azure resources. Creating users needs an Entra role, such as User Administrator.
No. Updates run in the background and can take a while.

misconceptions.myth: A deleted user is gone straight away.
misconceptions.reality: No. It stays in the recycle bin, and you can restore it for 30 days.

architectureDecisions: Use dynamic groups for access and licences: base the rule on HR details such as department or job title, so access follows people when they join, move or leave. Remember they need Entra ID P1.
Use assigned groups for exceptions: when a rule can't describe who belongs, such as a project team, let the group owner add people by hand.
Script bulk changes: use Microsoft Graph PowerShell or Azure CLI so the result is the same every time. Don't use the old AzureAD or MSOnline modules; they are retired.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give a new team accounts, then let groups do the work of keeping access up to date.

steps.label: New team
steps.title: Five people join the IT team on Monday
body: Each one needs an account. Each one needs access to the right Azure resources.
Giving access person by person is slow, and it is easy to forget to remove it when someone leaves.

steps.label: Users
steps.title: A user is an identity in Microsoft Entra ID
body: Microsoft Entra ID (the new name for Azure AD) is the directory that holds your users. A member user belongs to your organisation. A guest user is someone from outside, such as a partner, invited by email.
Useful properties: name, job title, department and usage location. Usage location is needed before you can give someone a licence directly.

callout.text: Fill in department and job title. Dynamic groups use these properties to decide who is in the group.

steps.label: Groups
steps.title: Two kinds of group
body: A security group is used to give access: assign an Azure role or an app to the group, not to each person.
A Microsoft 365 group adds a shared mailbox, calendar and Teams space. It can also be used for access, but its main job is collaboration.

steps.label: Dynamic
steps.title: Let a rule fill the group for you
body: With assigned membership, you add and remove people by hand. With dynamic membership, Entra adds everyone whose properties match a rule, for example department equals IT, and removes them when the property changes.
Dynamic groups need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence.

callout.text: You cannot add members by hand to a dynamic group. Change the user's properties or the rule instead.

steps.label: Bulk
steps.title: Case: the whole team on Monday
body: Upload a CSV file (Users > Bulk operations > Bulk create) to create all five accounts at once with department = IT.
The dynamic rule puts them in the IT security group within minutes, and that group already has the right Azure role.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Users and groups in one minute
body: Give access to groups, and let rules keep the groups correct.
recap: Member = your organisation; guest = invited outsider
Usage location is needed for direct licence assignment
Security groups for access; Microsoft 365 groups for collaboration
Dynamic membership uses a rule on user properties (needs P1)
Bulk create, invite and delete with a CSV file

handsOn.title: Create a user and a group, then add the user
handsOn.cost: Free. Users and groups cost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com with the account that created your Azure subscription. That account is a Global Administrator of its own Microsoft Entra tenant.

steps.do: In the portal search bar type 'Microsoft Entra ID' and open it. Note the 'Primary domain' on the Overview page (it ends in onmicrosoft.com).
steps.see: The Overview page with your tenant name, tenant ID and primary domain.

steps.do: Go to Users > New user > Create new user. User principal name: ana.lab, display name: Ana Lab. Tick 'Auto-generate password' and copy it somewhere safe.
steps.see: The Properties tab, where you can fill in job details.

steps.do: On the Properties tab set Job title: Cloud Engineer, Department: IT, Usage location: United Arab Emirates (or your country). Select Review + create > Create.
steps.see: Ana Lab in the users list after a refresh.

steps.do: Go to Groups > New group. Group type: Security, name: grp-it-lab, membership type: Assigned. Under Members, add Ana Lab. Select Create.
steps.tip: Dynamic membership needs a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence or trial. If Dynamic User is not offered, or the group cannot be saved, start the free trial in the licences lab first.

steps.see: Ana Lab listed as a direct member.
grp-it-lab listed. Membership works in both directions.

steps.do: Optional, needs a P1 trial (see the licences lab): create a second group, membership type Dynamic User, and add the rule user.department -eq "IT".
steps.see: Ana appears in the dynamic group after a few minutes, without being added by hand.

check: Ana Lab exists with department IT and a usage location.
cleanup: Keep Ana and the group for the next labs (licences, SSPR, RBAC). Delete them when you finish the identity labs: Users > select > Delete; Groups > select > Delete.
